checks.name: two-additive-records
checks.summary: A13, PASSED. Exactly two additive types were added beside Repository, RepositoryObservation and RequirementRepositoryLink: PublicationIntent (repository_id, locator, ref, base_branch, base_commit, head_commit, head_tree, changed_paths) which is serialised as the Outbox Item's Payload, and PublicationObservation (operation_id, repository_id, ref, published_commit, published_tree, local_commit, local_tree, trees_agree, state, reason, observed_at) which is write-once per operation identifier. The field lists are asserted from the AST, in order, so a silent addition fails. NEITHER record stores a URL, asserted as an absence over both field lists, and no existing aggregate grew a publication field. model.go's generic Validate and Decide type switches were not extended: the two records carry their own ValidatePublicationIntent and ValidatePublicationObservation, following control.go/lease.go/release.go and the RepositoryObservation precedent in the same file.

checks.name: closed-state-vocabulary
checks.summary: A14 and A21(iii), PASSED. The closed set has exactly five values: unobserved, published-and-observed, converged-on-existing-ref, ref-disagrees, refused-before-write. unobserved is a first-class value so nothing measured is ever reported as a plausible-looking value that was never measured, and published-and-observed is the terminal success value. The test asserts that no state contains complete, resolv, accept, done, finish or success as a substring, and that ValidPublicationState refuses the empty string and each of completed, done, accepted, resolved and published. This is the LEXICAL third of the three-way guarantee that a published branch is not a finished Requirement.

checks.name: ref-naming-rule
checks.summary: A19's pure half, PASSED. domain.PublicationRefName is the only producer of a ref name in the repository and is a deterministic function of the increment and execution identifiers: the same pair yields the same ref on repeated calls, a second Execution of the same Increment gets a different ref, and ten malformed identifier pairs plus ten refs outside the reserved prefix are each refused with ErrInvalidPublicationRef. ParsePublicationRef is the inverse READ, not a second producer, and is what the Firestore adapter uses to project the increment id into its single indexed field so the record itself carries no duplicate of it.

checks.name: observation-refuses-unmeasured-success
checks.summary: PASSED. A successful publication Observation must carry both the published and the local object names and an agreeing tree; eleven individual mutations are each refused, including an unknown state, a missing reason, a missing instant, a malformed object name, a success with no published object, a success with disagreeing trees and a success with the agreement flag cleared. An unobserved Observation is accepted and is refused the moment it carries a published tree. The intent refuses ten mutations including an unnormalised locator, a ref outside the reserved prefix, a head commit equal to the base commit and a zero or negative changed-path count.
